← paydayloandebt.org home

Rhode Island Payday Loan Laws: Legal Status [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Rhode Island residents.

Rhode Island Payday Loan Status

Rhode Island allows payday lending with regulation. $500 max; 10% of amount advanced Rollover practice: 1 rollover allowed

RuleRhode Island Status

Legal statusLEGAL

Loan / fee cap$500 max; 10% of amount advanced

Rollover rule1 rollover allowed

APR disclosureAPR disclosure required per TILA

Primary citationR.I. Gen. Laws 19-14.4-4

Usury Cap and Enforceability in Rhode Island

In Rhode Island, the state usury law controls what fees a lender can legally charge. Loans that exceed the cap may be:

Void in whole or in part - some states void usurious loans entirely; others require repayment of principal only, with no interest or fees.

Subject to statutory penalty - many states allow recovery of 2x or 3x the usurious interest paid.

Unenforceable via collection - a lawsuit on a usurious loan can itself be an FDCPA violation.

If you suspect a Rhode Island payday loan violates the cap, demand a full billing history and compare the effective APR (including all fees) against R.I. Gen. Laws 19-14.4-4.

Rollover Prohibitions in Rhode Island

1 rollover allowed

Rollovers are the mechanism by which payday lenders convert a 2-week loan into a multi-year debt trap. Each rollover typically requires a new fee equal to the original charge, so a $500 loan at 15% fee rolled 6 times costs $450 in fees alone - 90% of the original principal.

Most regulated states now limit rollovers or require cooling-off periods:

Database check. States like Florida, Kentucky, and Michigan require lenders to check a state database before issuing a new loan.

Cooling-off periods. Waiting periods (24 hours to 30 days) between loans.

Loan caps. Maximum number of loans per borrower per year.

If a Rhode Island lender rolled a loan without authority under R.I. Gen. Laws 19-14.4-4, the rollover may be void.

APR Disclosure Rules in Rhode Island

APR disclosure required per TILA

The federal Truth in Lending Act (TILA, 15 U.S.C. 1601) requires all lenders - including payday lenders in every state - to disclose the annual percentage rate before the loan is funded. Failure to disclose APR is itself a federal statutory violation with:

Actual damages

Statutory damages up to $5,000 (for closed-end credit)

Attorney-fee shifting

A typical 14-day payday loan with a 15% fee has an APR of roughly 391%. Lenders must disclose that number, not the "15%" fee alone.

ACH Revocation Rights - Applies in Rhode Island

Under Regulation E (12 CFR 1005) of the federal Electronic Fund Transfer Act, you can revoke ACH authorization at any time in writing - no state can override this federal right. The process:

Send written revocation to the lender and to your bank.

Bank must honor the revocation within 3 business days.

Any withdrawal after revocation is an unauthorized transfer.

See our ACH revocation guide for a template letter that works in all 50 states.

Military Lending Act Overlay (applies in Rhode Island)

If you are active-duty military or a covered dependent, the Military Lending Act (10 U.S.C. 987) caps consumer credit at 36% Military APR in every state, including Rhode Island. Violations carry criminal penalties.

Critical MLA protections:

36% all-in APR cap

No mandatory arbitration

No roll-over / refinancing

No prepayment penalty

Written disclosure required

See full MLA rights.

Bankruptcy Discharge of Payday Loans in Rhode Island

Payday loans are ordinarily dischargeable in bankruptcy. Exceptions:

Luxury goods within 90 days (11 U.S.C. 523(a)(2)(C)(i)(I)) - generally not an issue for payday advances, which are cash.

Cash advances over $1,000 within 70 days before filing (11 U.S.C. 523(a)(2)(C)(i)(II)) - presumptively non-dischargeable; courts can rebut with no-intent-to-deceive showing.

Fraudulent intent at origination - lender must sue within 60 days of 341 meeting under 11 U.S.C. 523(c).

For most Rhode Island debtors with ordinary payday debt, Chapter 7 discharges the loan within 90 days. See 1328(f) refiling screener and the Rhode Island means test.

Related Rhode Island Resources

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for South Dakota residents.

South Dakota Payday Loan Status

South Dakota is one of 10 states with an effective payday-loan cap. 36% APR cap (Initiated Measure 21, 2016) This makes traditional two-week payday lending economically unviable; lenders either exit the state or restructure as installment loans.

RuleSouth Dakota Status

Legal statusCAPPED

Loan / fee cap36% APR cap (Initiated Measure 21, 2016)

Cash advances over $1,000 within 70 days before filing (11 U.S.C. 523(a)(2)(C)(i)(II)) - presumptively non-dischargeable; courts can rebut with no-intent-to-deceive showing.

Fraudulent intent at origination - lender must sue within 60 days of 341 meeting under 11 U.S.C. 523(c).

For most Utah debtors with ordinary payday debt, Chapter 7 discharges the loan within 90 days. See 1328(f) refiling screener and the Utah means test.

## Vermont Payday Loan Laws: Banned Status [2026]
Source: https://paydayloandebt.org/states/vermont.html

← paydayloandebt.org home

Vermont Payday Loan Laws: Banned Status [2026]

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Vermont residents.

Vermont Payday Loan Status

Vermont is one of 18 states that ban payday lending. Consumer usury cap 18% blocks payday lending If a payday lender solicited or loaned to you in Vermont, the loan may be void or unenforceable, and you may have claims under state usury law.

RuleVermont Status

Legal statusBANNED

Loan / fee capConsumer usury cap 18% blocks payday lending

Rollover ruleN/A - banned

APR disclosureN/A

Primary citation9 V.S.A. 2201

Usury Cap and Enforceability in Vermont

In Vermont, the state usury law controls what fees a lender can legally charge. Loans that exceed the cap may be:

Void in whole or in part - some states void usurious loans entirely; others require repayment of principal only, with no interest or fees.

Subject to statutory penalty - many states allow recovery of 2x or 3x the usurious interest paid.

Unenforceable via collection - a lawsuit on a usurious loan can itself be an FDCPA violation.

If you suspect a Vermont payday loan violates the cap, demand a full billing history and compare the effective APR (including all fees) against 9 V.S.A. 2201.

Rollover Prohibitions in Vermont

N/A - banned

Rollovers are the mechanism by which payday lenders convert a 2-week loan into a multi-year debt trap. Each rollover typically requires a new fee equal to the original charge, so a $500 loan at 15% fee rolled 6 times costs $450 in fees alone - 90% of the original principal.

Most regulated states now limit rollovers or require cooling-off periods:

Database check. States like Florida, Kentucky, and Michigan require lenders to check a state database before issuing a new loan.

Cooling-off periods. Waiting periods (24 hours to 30 days) between loans.

Loan caps. Maximum number of loans per borrower per year.

If a Vermont lender rolled a loan without authority under 9 V.S.A. 2201, the rollover may be void.

APR Disclosure Rules in Vermont

N/A

The federal Truth in Lending Act (TILA, 15 U.S.C. 1601) requires all lenders - including payday lenders in every state - to disclose the annual percentage rate before the loan is funded. Failure to disclose APR is itself a federal statutory violation with:

Actual damages

Statutory damages up to $5,000 (for closed-end credit)

Attorney-fee shifting

A typical 14-day payday loan with a 15% fee has an APR of roughly 391%. Lenders must disclose that number, not the "15%" fee alone.

ACH Revocation Rights - Applies in Vermont

Under Regulation E (12 CFR 1005) of the federal Electronic Fund Transfer Act, you can revoke ACH authorization at any time in writing - no state can override this federal right. The process:

Send written revocation to the lender and to your bank.

Bank must honor the revocation within 3 business days.

Any withdrawal after revocation is an unauthorized transfer.

See our ACH revocation guide for a template letter that works in all 50 states.

Military Lending Act Overlay (applies in Vermont)

If you are active-duty military or a covered dependent, the Military Lending Act (10 U.S.C. 987) caps consumer credit at 36% Military APR in every state, including Vermont. Violations carry criminal penalties.

Critical MLA protections:

36% all-in APR cap

No mandatory arbitration

No roll-over / refinancing

No prepayment penalty

Written disclosure required

See full MLA rights.

Bankruptcy Discharge of Payday Loans in Vermont

Payday loans are ordinarily dischargeable in bankruptcy. Exceptions:

Luxury goods within 90 days (11 U.S.C. 523(a)(2)(C)(i)(I)) - generally not an issue for payday advances, which are cash.

Cash advances over $1,000 within 70 days before filing (11 U.S.C. 523(a)(2)(C)(i)(II)) - presumptively non-dischargeable; courts can rebut with no-intent-to-deceive showing.

Fraudulent intent at origination - lender must sue within 60 days of 341 meeting under 11 U.S.C. 523(c).

For most Vermont debtors with ordinary payday debt, Chapter 7 discharges the loan within 90 days. See 1328(f) refiling screener and the Vermont means test.

Most regulated states now limit rollovers or require cooling-off periods:

Database check. States like Florida, Kentucky, and Michigan require lenders to check a state database before issuing a new loan.

Cooling-off periods. Waiting periods (24 hours to 30 days) between loans.

Loan caps. Maximum number of loans per borrower per year.

If a Wyoming lender rolled a loan without authority under W.S. 40-14-363, the rollover may be void.

APR Disclosure Rules in Wyoming

APR disclosure required per TILA

The federal Truth in Lending Act (TILA, 15 U.S.C. 1601) requires all lenders - including payday lenders in every state - to disclose the annual percentage rate before the loan is funded. Failure to disclose APR is itself a federal statutory violation with:

Actual damages

Statutory damages up to $5,000 (for closed-end credit)

Attorney-fee shifting

A typical 14-day payday loan with a 15% fee has an APR of roughly 391%. Lenders must disclose that number, not the "15%" fee alone.

ACH Revocation Rights - Applies in Wyoming

Under Regulation E (12 CFR 1005) of the federal Electronic Fund Transfer Act, you can revoke ACH authorization at any time in writing - no state can override this federal right. The process:

Send written revocation to the lender and to your bank.

Bank must honor the revocation within 3 business days.

Any withdrawal after revocation is an unauthorized transfer.

See our ACH revocation guide for a template letter that works in all 50 states.

Military Lending Act Overlay (applies in Wyoming)

If you are active-duty military or a covered dependent, the Military Lending Act (10 U.S.C. 987) caps consumer credit at 36% Military APR in every state, including Wyoming. Violations carry criminal penalties.

Critical MLA protections:

36% all-in APR cap

No mandatory arbitration

No roll-over / refinancing

No prepayment penalty

Written disclosure required

See full MLA rights.

Bankruptcy Discharge of Payday Loans in Wyoming

Payday loans are ordinarily dischargeable in bankruptcy. Exceptions:

Luxury goods within 90 days (11 U.S.C. 523(a)(2)(C)(i)(I)) - generally not an issue for payday advances, which are cash.

Cash advances over $1,000 within 70 days before filing (11 U.S.C. 523(a)(2)(C)(i)(II)) - presumptively non-dischargeable; courts can rebut with no-intent-to-deceive showing.

Fraudulent intent at origination - lender must sue within 60 days of 341 meeting under 11 U.S.C. 523(c).

For most Wyoming debtors with ordinary payday debt, Chapter 7 discharges the loan within 90 days. See 1328(f) refiling screener and the Wyoming means test.
